svg.title: Valley Floor cap and sock
svg.text: Valley Floor
A perforated five-panel cap and a merino crew sock. One number, worn like a bib: the elevation
every run, ride and skin track in this city starts from.

text.font-family: Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif
Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif

svg.text: Cap, wearer's left. Satin-stitch numerals 1.6 in tall, bib spacing, set low so the brim edge crops the baseline.

text.font-family: Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif
Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif

svg.text: Sock. Jacquard knit-in numerals, 1.75 in, up the back of the calf.
Sage arch band, Y-heel gore, hand-linked toe.

text.font-family: Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif
Oswald, 'Futura Extra Bold Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif

svg.text: Satin stitch over laser-perforated ripstop at 3:1. The holes run under the thread.
4,219 is the number on the airport sign. It is the valley floor, and everything
here is uphill from it. On the cap it is spaced like a race bib, because that is
what it is: the number you start with. On the sock it is knitted in, not printed,
and it faces whoever is behind you.
Cap: 85 gsm four-way stretch recycled ripstop, laser-perforated side and back panels,
reflective bound brim, Coolmax sweatband, elastic back, no hardware. Sock: 58/39/3
merino, nylon and elastane at 200 needles. Sold as a set in a glassine sleeve.
The salt-crystal icon lives on the sweatband label only.
Cream cap
Ink numerals
Navy sock
Sage arch band
Second run: Sky
